What Huli does

Huli scans printed books with your phone on a stand. It reads English and ʻōlelo Hawaiʻi, including the ʻokina and kahakō, fixes common Hawaiian reading mistakes, points out words it is unsure about, and exports a searchable PDF or a Word file.

Everything happens on your phone. Nothing is uploaded.

What you need

  •  A tripod or overhead stand, with the phone looking straight down at the book.
  •  A dark, matte cloth under the book, so the page edges stand out.
  •  Two lights, one on each side at about 45 degrees. A single lamp gives a yellow glow and shadows.
  •  Optional: a Bluetooth camera remote (it presses a volume key) and a sheet of glass to hold pages flat.

Scanning a book

1. New book. Tap Scan on the title page card to fill in the title and author, or type them. Choose the language, whether the book is printed with ʻokina and kahakō, and the layout.

2. Set up the page. Tap Detect page, drag the corners onto the page edges, and tap Confirm. Keep the page still while Huli locks focus and exposure.

3. Capture. The border is red while you turn a page, yellow while it settles, and green when it is ready. Press the remote, a volume key, or Capture. Turn on Auto to shoot every time the border stays green.

4. Keep going. Huli reads the pages in the background while you shoot.

Checking the text

  •  Tap a book to see its pages. Green means clean, amber shows words to check, red needs attention, and gray is blank.
  •  Tap a page to read its text. Tap any word to correct it. Switch to Image to compare with the photo, and pinch to zoom.
  •  Check words walks you through every doubtful word, one at a time, with ʻ ā ē ī ō ū buttons.
  •  If printed page numbers jump, Huli warns you and offers Reshoot.
  •  Long-press a page to reshoot it, insert a page after it, mark it blank, move it, or delete it.

Exporting

Tap Export to save a searchable PDF, a Word file, or both.

Tips

  •  Single page gives the sharpest text, which matters for small print and for ʻokina and kahakō. Two-page spread is faster.
  •  Bring the camera close enough that the page nearly fills the preview.
  •  Long-press the status label on the capture screen to adjust the capture settings.
  •  Reprocess all pages in a book’s menu reads every page again, for example after an update.

Open source

Huli is free and open source. Huli’s own code is released under the MIT License. It is built on MakeACopy by Christian Kierdorf, used under the Apache License 2.0, together with PaddleOCR, OpenCV and ONNX Runtime (Apache License 2.0). The Hawaiian word list comes from the Hawaiian Corpus Project (CC0) and the English word list from FrequencyWords (CC BY-SA 4.0).
